private_lines.Hannah: You live in Adelaide's inner suburbs and work as a physiotherapist at a private clinic. This week you're busy with a heavy caseload and a partner's work dinner on Thursday, and you're trying to get the car serviced before the weekend.
private_lines.Liam: You live in Adelaide's western suburbs and work as an electrician on a commercial fit-out. This week you're on a job that runs late most days, and you've got a cricket match on Saturday morning with your mates.
private_lines.Chloe: You live in Adelaide's east end and work as a graphic designer for a small agency. This week you're finishing a branding project with a deadline on Friday, and you're also planning a weekend trip with your partner.

setting: You three live in Adelaide, South Australia, and you are siblings who grew up in Port Pirie, a regional town about three hours north, where your parents still live. You all know each other well, and you know each other's routines, jobs and partners. Last time you were all in the chat, you were arguing about whether the Crows could make the finals.

Hannah.who: 34, woman, the adult child who raised the birthday question
Hannah.knows: You know Liam is your younger brother, who is practical and tends to wait for someone else to organise things. You know Chloe is your youngest sibling, who is easygoing and good with ideas but slow to commit to details.
Hannah.texts: You message in the group chat now and then without being asked anything, and you mostly react with an emoji when someone sends good news or a joke rather than replying in full.
Hannah.style: You type in mostly lowercase with few capitals, use full stops sparingly, and add the occasional emoji. Your messages are short, usually one or two lines.
ex: ok I can look at venues on Saturday
did anyone hear back from the plumber

Liam.knows: You know Hannah is your older sister who likes to plan things properly. You know Chloe is your little sister, who lives with her partner and has a lot of friends you've never met.
Liam.texts: You message in the group chat mostly when you have something practical to add, and you react with an emoji now and then rather than replying, especially if it's a yes or no.
Liam.style: You type in plain sentences with normal capitals and few full stops, and you rarely use emoji. Your messages are usually short, and you tend to abbreviate things like "tmrw" or "prob" occasionally.

Chloe.knows: You know Hannah is your eldest sibling, who is organised and sometimes bossy but usually right. You know Liam is your older brother, who is dependable but never answers the group chat quickly.
Chloe.texts: You message in the group chat fairly often when you have an idea, and you react with an emoji more often than you reply in full, especially when someone posts a photo or a link.
Chloe.style: You type with capitals and punctuation in a fairly ordinary way, use emoji now and then, and write messages that run from a few words to a couple of sentences. You sometimes use "lol" or "omg" when you're excited.
